milestone: Per-tick native editor playback and committed input traces
implemented: Native WorldSession::advance_tick validates session/tick/input guards, commits one tick and services queued saves, returning fixed-size replacement metadata without JSON, UUIDs or public retry receipts.
Automatic editor catch-up commits each tick independently, retaining successful predecessors when a later tick fails; explicit multi-tick RPC requests preserve whole-batch rollback.
Input preparation precedes simulation; allocation-free noexcept commit consumes edges/mouse backlog only after success. Held movement and evaluator analog rates remain per-tick.
The last controlled poll retains a bounded exact committed input sequence and its legacy first-frame metadata; failed ticks never enter the trace.
Gameplay saves execute after their requesting automatic tick; a load stops catch-up, opens a fresh paused session and clears old input. Storage service time is excluded from subsequent catch-up.

final_native_receipt_test.note: After the full runtime run, strengthened only the native test to retain an explicit receipt across forty automatic ticks; rebuilt and reran that test. Production source/binaries unchanged.

windows_runs.name: tick-playback-headless
coverage: Playback/view schemas are discoverable; invalid camera selection is atomic and Game excludes Scene interaction tools.
Paused clock and detached draw remain inert; Step advances exactly once with core receipt retry and strict session guards.
Only owner poll advances real time; long stalls cap at eight ticks, competing runtime mutations reject, and paused wall time never catches up.
Existing runtime.start/stop synchronize with the desktop driver, defaulting external starts to paused.
Game uses the same runtime with its frozen camera lens and hierarchy despite authored camera edits and deletion.
A genuine animation sampling failure preserves automatic ticks15–17 and pauses before18; explicit four-tick Step still rolls back all state, with unchanged authored bytes/history.

windows_runs.name: tick-input-headless
coverage: Frozen controller discovery and strict playing/Game-camera focus gates work without requiring graphics.
Real controller movement/jump/yaw matches evaluated controls; held movement persists, while look/jump/use consume once and repeat events/receipts cannot retrigger them.
Invalid batches validate atomically; reserved/gamepad/type/shape/count errors preserve pending input and failed receipts are reusable.
Eight-tick catch-up drains independent mouse frames -180/-180/-70 then zero, preserves held movement, and consumes jump/use once; exact frames feed independent replay.
Focus loss, Pause and Scene switch clear held controls and pending edges; explicit reacquisition does not restore stale movement.
Persisted rebound profile changes actual movement and yaw/pitch; stale profile revisions reject without disturbing the old evaluator.
Stop/new session drops configuration and rejects stale events; independent semantic replay exactly matches final controller/camera state with unchanged authored bytes/history.
After actual recursive authored deletion, frozen runtime controller/camera discovery, configuration and movement remain valid; Stop restores the now-empty authored controller list.

windows_runs.name: tick-gameplay-save-headless
coverage: Automatic playback commits a Tick-zero save exactly at tick1, independently of later due ticks in the same poll.
External save mutations remain rejected while playing through both direct C ABI and local IPC.
A later real game callback observes terminal completion and clears its pending state without repeating the write.
Automatic game load adopts a fresh paused session, clears native input/clock/module caches and leaves authoring and save bytes unchanged.
Paused step exposes source/current replacement metadata; exact old-session retry is inert and restored saved tokens do not reenact commands.
Explicit four-tick batch failure restores complete C# and controller state and performs no durable save.
Automatic failure preserves its first three C#/physics ticks and first-tick durable save; movement persists while look/jump/use consume once, then input clears.
Explicit recovery resumes from the committed prefix without replaying old input, failed callbacks or completed saves.

native_test_coverage: 120 typed-versus-one-tick-RPC comparisons preserve controller, camera and dynamic-body state exactly.
Closed/inactive/wrong-session/stale-tick/invalid-input guards reject without mutation; typed ticks do not allocate or evict public RPC receipts.
A real Jolt contact-capacity failure rolls back body state and tick, with failure/rollback scopes recorded.
Input commit runs with global allocation refusal and noexcept assertions; backlog, held keys, edges, neutral gating and stick-rate semantics pass.

limitations: Per-tick automatic commits intentionally differ from explicit multi-tick all-or-nothing requests. Earlier successful saves cannot be undone by a later automatic failure.
The input trace covers at most the most recent eight committed controlled ticks; it is not retained simulation history or a general replay recording system.
Editor physical gamepad acquisition and native audio output remain unconnected. This establishes their tick boundary, not completed device integration.
Native owner, storage and presentation remain synchronous. No new asynchronous scheduler, sustained frame-time, game-performance or checkpoint-overhead claim.
Windows HWND and semantic Avalonia tests use synthetic events. The session was locked; no OS screenshot, physical input feel, general DPI/IME/accessibility or power-loss qualification.
Both GPUs are on one laptop; broad shipped-game hardware, Linux hardware rendering and console qualification remain unfinished.
